title: Air-gapped registry sync and upgrade runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for executing air-gapped installs and in-place upgrades for Redwood Private deployments. Focus: creating and validating offline registries, building dependency bundles (container images, helm charts, OS packages, language artifacts), and the terraform module considerations to wire up the network/VMs and HA storage for an upgrade window.

Status / context:
- Draft: consolidates recent experiments with skopeo/crane + OCI archives, Harbor offline sync, and terraform module tweaks for registry endpoints.
- Not yet tested end-to-end in a customer environment (lab runs completed).
- Goal: be able to perform a full minor and patch upgrade with no internet access from target cluster nodes.

High-level flow:
1) Pre-flight prep (local workstation or mirror host with internet)
2) Mirror artifacts into an air-gapped registry / artifact bundle
3) Ship bundle (tarball / disk / secure transfer) to customer network or import into customer mirror host
4) Validate registry + package availability in target environment
5) Run terraform to provision upgrade staging nodes and apply kube/helm changes
6) Perform rolling upgrade with smoke tests and rollback if needed

Pre-flight checklist (local):
- [ ] Confirm target cluster k8s version and current Redwood Private component versions (api-server, control-plane services, redis/minio/postgres images).
- [ ] Collect list of images: service images, sidecars, envoy/proxy, monitoring (prometheus, grafana), logging (fluentd).
- [ ] Collect list of helm charts + chart dependencies and exact chart versions.
- [ ] Collect list of OS packages (yum/apt), pip wheels, maven jars, npm packages required by bootstrap scripts or init containers.
- [ ] Evaluate image signing requirements (cosign). Export public keys if customer expects signature verification.
- [ ] Ensure storage for bundle >= estimated size + 20%. Estimate: sum of compressed image sizes + charts + language artifacts.

Artifact mirror patterns (tools we used):
- Container images: skopeo copy / crane pull + oci-archive
  - Example skopeo: skopeo sync --src docker --dest dir --dest-tls-verify=false --all "docker://ghcr.io/redwood-inference/..." 
  - Example to produce oci archive: crane export ghcr.io/redwood-inference/service:1.2.0 service-1.2.0.tar
- OCI registry mirror: Harbor or GitLab Container Registry in air-gapped mode. Use Harbor import function or crictl ctr image import to load image tarballs on nodes.
- Helm charts: helm pull <chart> --version x.y.z --untar && package into charts/ index.yaml with helm repo index . --url "file://localcharts"
- OS packages: apt-mirror / reposync for yum. For Debian/Ubuntu build Release + Packages indices and include GPG keys for apt.
- Language packages: pip download -r requirements.txt --dest wheelhouse/; mvn dependency:go-offline; npm pack for critical packages.

Bundle layout recommendation (tarball structure):
- bundle-<env>-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz
  - registry/ (OCI tar archives OR docker-loader formatted tars)
  - charts/ (packaged .tgz and index.yaml)
  - apt/ or yum/ (mirror root with Release and Packages files)
  - language/ (wheelhouse/, maven-offline/, npm-offline/)
  - signatures/ (cosign signatures for images, checksum files)
  - manifest.json (list of artifacts, checksums, instructions)

manifest.json (example content to include as plain text in bundle):
- a flattened list with fields: artifact_type,image_or_path,version,sha256,notes
(We keep a TSV inside the manifest because some air-gapped customers prefer simple parsing).

Registry import on air-gapped mirror host (customer side):
- Option A (Harbor import): use Harbor UI or API to import OCI tarballs into project.
- Option B (containerd nodes): ctr -n k8s.io images import /path/to/service-1.2.0.tar && crane digest to verify.
- Option C (local distribution registry): docker load < tar && docker push to local-registry:5000/project/service:1.2.0 (requires docker on mirror host).

Image signing and trust:
- If cosign verification is enabled in cluster admission, bring public cosign key(s) in signatures/ and import to the cluster policy (imagePolicy).
- If digest pinning is used, ensure manifest includes digest pins to avoid mutable tags.

Terraform module notes (draft):
- Module: modules/private_registry
  - purpose: provision VM(s) for mirror host, attach storage, create firewall rules for internal registry endpoints.
  - input vars (recommended):
    - mirror_vm_count (default 1)
    - mirror_vm_size
    - mirror_disk_gb
    - allowed_sources (list of internal CIDRs)
    - ssl_certificate_id (optional) -- if customer wants TLS fronting
    - registry_username, registry_password (sensitive)
  - outputs:
    - registry_endpoint (url)
    - registry_host_ips (list)
  - notes: include optional data_source to populate AMI/image ID for hardened VM. Provide a null_resource that runs remote-exec to unpack initial bundle into /var/registry-mirror and trigger import scripts.
- Module: modules/upgrade_staging
  - purpose: spin up a small set of staging nodes (tainted) to validate new images/helm charts before rolling to control-plane nodes.
  - important var: staging_node_count default 2. Add provisioner to run smoke tests after terraform apply.

Terraform gotchas for air-gapped customers:
- Avoid creating resources that require public provider plugins to download during apply. Lock providers in a private plugin mirror or vendor providers using Terraform Plugin Cache.
- Use remote-exec only with files already present on the VM or run scripts that are part of the bundle; do not curl from the internet.
- Secrets management: prefer customer KMS + pre-created service account keys shipped in bundle, or use an interactive step to paste secrets during apply.

Upgrade plan (minor/patch):
1) Backup phase:
   - Backup Postgres dump (pg_dump) and wal archives. Verify backup locally (restore to a test instance).
   - Snapshot object storage (MinIO) if used for stateful artifacts.
   - Export Redis RDB if Redis used for ephemeral state that must be preserved.
2) Staging validation (on staging nodes provisioned via terraform module):
   - Import new images into registry_endpoint and ensure image pull by staging kubelets.
   - Apply helm charts in a staging namespace with the same values file as prod.
   - Run a smoke test harness (smoke.sh) that tests health endpoints and a small end-to-end prompt through local model endpoint.
3) Control-plane upgrade (rolling):
   - Drain one control-plane node at a time (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data).
   - Upgrade control-plane components in-place: apply new helm chart for core control-plane pods, wait for readiness checks.
   - Validate apiserver responds and cluster autoscaler (if present) is stable.
4) Worker upgrade (rolling with surge):
   - Cordon one worker, drain workloads per pod disruption budget policy, update daemonsets and deployments.
   - Uncordon after validating pods reach Ready.
5) Post-upgrade validation:
   - Run integration tests, latency tests (token generation smoke), cost/throughput sanity checks vs baseline.
   - Check logs for OOM, image pull errors, crashloops.

Rollback plan (quick):
- If a critical failure happens during control-plane upgrade, revert helm release to previous chart version (helm rollback) and restore Postgres from backup if DB schema changed.
- If image-related: update deployments to point to previous digest and redeploy.
- If registry import is missing critical images, trigger manual image import from bundle on mirror host and re-trigger pod restarts.

Validation & health checks (commands to run):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl get pods -A | grep -E "CrashLoop|ImagePullBackOff"
- curl -sS --unix-socket /var/run/control-plane.sock http://localhost/healthz
- for image in $(cat manifest.tsv | cut -f2); do crane digest $image; done  # validate digest availability locally

Notes from experiments (lessons learned):
- OCI archive approach (crane export/import) is smaller on disk vs full registry mirror for some layers because dedupe is good, but it loses registry metadata unless you store manifest -> we now always include a manifest with digest pins.
- Harbor's import UI is convenient for manual customer ops but automation for large bundles is slower; the API + parallel imports work better.
- Some customers prefer 'git-lfs like' storage for charts; we standardized on packaging charts as tgz and shipping index.yaml in bundle.
- Terraform remote-exec that runs 'docker load' on the mirror host is fragile. Better: run an init script from the mirror host's local filesystem that is idempotent and logs progress under /var/log/airgap-import.log.

Outstanding decisions / TODOs:
- Decide on a canonical schema for manifest.tsv (columns + required fields).
- Add a terraform null_resource that verifies signature files (cosign) after import and fails if any image is unsigned when policy requires it.
- Define retention policy for offline mirror images and prune process; add to the runbook.
- Add a lightweight GUI checklist (json->HTML) we can hand to PMs during upgrades.

Appendix: quick commands and example snippets
- Create wheelhouse:
  pip download -r requirements.txt --dest wheelhouse/
- Export images with crane (recommended for reproducible digests):
  crane export ghcr.io/redwood-inference/service:1.2.0 /tmp/service-1.2.0.tar
- Import into containerd on mirror host:
  sudo ctr -n k8s.io images import /tmp/service-1.2.0.tar && sudo ctr -n k8s.io images tag "sha256:<digest>" local-registry:5000/project/service:1.2.0
- Example terraform snippet (module usage):
  module "mirror" {
    source = "./modules/private_registry"
    mirror_vm_count = 1
    mirror_vm_size = "m4.large"
    mirror_disk_gb = 500
    allowed_sources = ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  }

Contact: Maya Alvarez (owner) — primary for playbook; escalate to Priya for terraform module reviews, Ethan for registry import automation.

Changelog:
- 2024-11-07 created initial draft from lab notes
- 2024-12-12 added terraform module skeleton and staging plan
- 2025-01-14 added rollback steps, signature notes, and bundle manifest recommendation

End of document.
